chapter: Desvigne compared; Piron, Celestin and rivals
title: The Piron band at the roof garden
summary: He recalls Piron's sweet, concert-style violin band of about twelve pieces on Gravier roof garden.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: But for solo, sitting there with his arm, solo. Did you ever hear the P-Rone band? I heard the P-Rone band once or twice. They was playing on a roof garden here. Oh, up there on the Gravier about? Yeah, Gravier. That was his favorite spot. He had that spot sold up. And whenever it would be a dance up at the roof garden, it would be P-Rone. Remember who was the drummer? I don't know who was the drummer for P-Rone at that time.
There was one man, you know, Louis Cartrell's father, the old man Cartrell, Louis Cartrell. They played with P-Rone a long time. I just wondered if you remembered hearing him. I don't know.
I don't know. He had no man. But I'm going to see.
What did the band sound like? What's the type of band?

P-Rone had more of a concert band. His band was more of a soft music style. Like you hear those guys say, Guy Lombard, the Swedish music this side ever. P-Rone had one of the bands with the Swedish music this side ever. He had one of the bands with the Swedish music this side ever. P-Rone had one of the bands with the Swedish music. He was a violin player. Yes, I never got to hear him. I never got to meet him. He was one of the little cripple fellow, one of the little violin players. His band never was no hot band or no soul, but it was a sweet musical band. He played a lot of sweet music. He played a lot of sweet music, concert music. How big a band was it? Remember, there wasn't as big as Sidney's. It wasn't as big as Sidney's. It wasn't as big as Sidney's. He had about twelve pieces. It was a pretty big band. Yeah, a pretty big band. He had about twelve pieces. At that time, the big band was on the raise at the time. stuff like Walter Barnes, like Walter Barnes, where Walter Barnes got killed in a fire.
